classes.title: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.label: Genesis 2:7
precepts.why:
God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”. God's image is the greatest image there is, and he mirrored man after himself, then gave him dominion and rulership. “And God blessed them”. But the blessing did not end with his image and dominion. In chapter 2, “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.”

The breath of life is wisdom, and it is what activated us. The word of God has to activate your life. God gave us laws to govern us so that we could be that special people; without them we would be just like every other nation. We are at the lowest state right now because we sinned against God, but we do not want to share power with any nation or be all-inclusive. God wants all or none, and we wait in this state until he puts us back in our rightful place.

Wisdom of Solomon 7 shows what that breath is. Wisdom, “which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit”. That is why we understand the Bible and have a scripture for everything we say. She is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care, having all power, overseeing all things”. Free from care means free from the cares of this world. Mark 4 names them: “the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” Wisdom says beware of covetousness, so you do not entertain it.

Then the verse that ties it to Genesis 2: “For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Wisdom flows down from the Almighty and molds you, so if she is influencing you, you are tethered to God. Otherwise something else, covetousness or lust, is influencing you. That breath is what God gave us in Genesis 2, and we let something else draw us away. God gave us everything, and we were led away by women, money, riches and cars, as if the things he created were greater than him.

The power of God is his word. Hebrews 4 says “the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword”, the same words used of wisdom, and it “is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” Psalms 19 names the pure influence: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” “the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” We were once simple; now wisdom makes us wise and we see clearly. In 1 Samuel 10:6 the Spirit of the Lord comes and a man is “turned into another man.”

Much is given, so much is required. Christ asks, “why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” The one who hears and does is like the man who “laid the foundation on a rock”, and that foundation lets you endure tribulation; the one who hears and does not is the house that falls. Learn yourself before chasing deep prophecy: get off the sin first. Wisdom is “the unspotted mirror of the power of God”, and James says pure religion is “to keep himself unspotted from the world.” “remaining in herself, she maketh all things new”. Tether yourself to wisdom and she makes you new.

People are watching. A sister came to the truth because she saw the camp in the streets and not one brother tried to talk to her. That is the right example: a people made in God's image, living by the breath he gave, set apart from every other nation.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 9:9
precepts.why:
“the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man.” His master saw that the Lord was with him and made him overseer over his house, and “the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake.” And “Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured”: he had a very good reputation, and people looked at him as a man of integrity and good character.

Then his master’s wife “cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.” He refused: his master had committed all that he had to his hand, “neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?” Nobody was watching him. He could have done it, but he said no. That is where integrity comes from: making the right decision when nobody is watching.

Ecclesiasticus 9:9 gives the same wisdom as a command: “Sit not at all with another man’s wife, nor sit down with her in thine arms, and spend not thy money with her at the wine; lest thine heart incline unto her, and so through thy desire thou fall into destruction.” Do not sit with another man’s wife at all. Do not play with it. Do not be drinking around somebody else’s wife, because your heart will incline to her, and both of you will destroy everything.

Joseph lived that. When “there was none of the men of the house there within,” she caught him by his garment, “and he left his garment in her hand, and fled.” He knew it was wickedness that would destroy his reputation and everything he had worked so hard for, and that he would not only be sinning against her but against the Lord. He fled rather than sit with it, even though he went to prison when she lied on him.

precepts.label: Isaiah 41:14
precepts.why:
The Bible says God is a man of war. War is coming to this place; God is bringing war to the earth. And we should not be afraid of it. Isaiah 41: “For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee. Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel; I will help thee, saith the Lord, and thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel”. God is talking to us. Don't be afraid; he is going to help us.

Read on: “Behold, I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth: thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and shalt make the hills as chaff”. A new sharp threshing instrument is a weapon, a weapon of war. The mountains are the nations, and we are going to beat them small. “Thou shalt fan them, and the wind shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them”. A time is coming when we will say, there was a place named America; what happened to it? It will be wiped out and never remembered again.

So when war comes, we should be celebrating, happy, not sad, because through those wars our salvation and our freedom come. We should pray for that thing. Our job now is to prepare for it, spiritually and mentally, not physically: prepare ourselves and our people, and keep a food pantry, as Bishop has been teaching for a while.

That preparing is spiritual warfare: “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh”; the weapons of our warfare are “mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. Don't get caught up in the foolishness of this place, the marches and the stupidity, even with your own family. Stay in the scripture, cast down every evil imagination in the minds of our people, and bring every thought “to the obedience of Christ”, the black Messiah. The man of war fights for us.

thread.text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.

classes.title: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.label: 2 Peter 1:4-5
precepts.why:
To covet is not simply to desire. It is to want what belongs to another inordinately: you violate God's laws to get it. “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s”. The daughter belongs under the father just like everything else in his house. Go around him to get her, never telling the fathers or the elders, and you have coveted. To entice is to allure, to bait, to induce to evil; it is trickery and deception. “My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not”. And “Love worketh no ill to his neighbour”: if you love the sister, how did you use ill means to get her?

Peter shows what we are supposed to be doing instead: “Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust. And beside this, giving all diligence”.

As brothers and sisters come in here, you are supposed to be escaping these worldly elements and truly repenting. When you look across the aisle, you are supposed to be looking for righteousness, not just her behind. Taking your sister for lust is the corruption that is in the world, and the same thing goes on on the other side. A man who talks to you under cover, without your father and without the leadership, does not have good intentions; the fact that he didn't do it the right way shows you where his mind is.

Do it with diligence, the right way. When we announce our marriages we say, this is the day the Lord has made between you two; you can bring forth righteousness right here, and the Lord, the angels and everybody are in agreement with it. When you do things the right way, you have a whole community behind you. The fathers and the elders have the vantage point: we see down the road where it is going, and we make the decision as fathers.

thread.text: If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.

classes.title: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.label: Leviticus 6:4-5
precepts.why:
Exodus 22:17: “If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins”. He has to pay, but he still is not getting the daughter. Somebody might say, he paid, so he gets to take her. Leviticus 6 shows the principle: “Then it shall be, because he hath sinned, and is guilty, that he shall restore that which he took violently away”.

Took violently away. To entice that daughter against her father's wishes is to violate him, and violation is violence. That is the same reason a man who steals an ox must “restore five oxen for an ox”: the owner was violated, and restitution is paid for the violent act against him.

“or the thing which he hath deceitfully gotten”. The recent matter was deceit. Her fathers didn't know anything about it, the leadership didn't know anything about it, nobody knew until her sister discovered it, and they still weren't going to say anything. How are you going to come up later saying, here's the law?

“Or all that about which he hath sworn falsely; he shall even restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto, and give it unto him to whom it appertaineth, in the day of his trespass offering”. The principal is the actual thing taken, and the fifth part is added on top. So you are not getting the daughter, and you still have to pay the fathers. That is why the judgment goes forward: we will not leave that kind of example for the rest of the sisters, to be beguiled by a wicked brother who says we're applying Exodus 22:16. That's a damn lie.

precepts.label: Matthew 19:3-8
precepts.why:
The Pharisees came to Christ “tempting him, and saying unto him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?” They were trying to use Moses' law, the writing of divorcement in Deuteronomy 24. Christ took them back to the beginning: “Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female, And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh?” From the beginning there was no such thing as divorce. What are you talking about, quoting Moses? It's the same as a negro trying to quote Exodus 22:16.

“Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder”. God did not put these backdoor marriages together. That's why love worketh no ill to his neighbour: you will not do evil and call yourself love. You don't love anything but your own lust.

“Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away? He saith unto them, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so”. The only reason Moses had to bring in that negro-proof law is that we were hard-headed and gave Moses hell. It is a failsafe law, a kind of bylaw to keep us from going all the way wicked. You are not supposed to be in failure at all for it even to come up, and quoting one after you went off and did wrong does not make you righteous.

That is covering violence with the garment: “for one covereth violence with his garment, saith the Lord of hosts: therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously”. The Pharisees enlarged the borders of their garments, and the fringes represent the laws. A man who deceived to get a sister and then gives her a so-called law from the Bible is covering his violation with the law. Sisters and brothers, watch yourselves, hold yourselves in the diligence of the scriptures, and stop playing games.

thread.label: Leviticus 17:11
thread.text: For the life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.

classes.title: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.label: Romans 5:10-11
precepts.why:
Leviticus says what the blood is for: “it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.” Paul shows whose blood: “For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.” When we were breaking God's law, we became his enemies. Being reconciled now, by Christ's life we are going to be saved.

“And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.” The blood of Christ is what gave us the atonement, so that we can build upon grace. The blood of Christ is more powerful than the animal sacrifice; it is the most powerful thing in this universe.

Read on in the chapter: “For if by one man’s offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.” By one man's offence death came into the world because of sin, and it reigned from then until today; look at our condition. “For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.”

That is the platform we have now. The platform we had under the one man's sin, we got messed up on. But Christ did it right this time, so we can build upon him and do it right because he did it right. It is through mercy we make it to the door, because our righteousness is as filthy rags; so nobody should be boasting of how perfect he is. Christ did not come for the righteous; he came for the sick, so he could heal them. And “in bringing many sons unto glory”, his death brings many sons into glory: a new body and a new mindset. So keep on trying, keep on working, and don't give up.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:2
precepts.why:
“And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.” Christ gave himself as a sacrifice for us. His blood on the altar is the atonement Leviticus speaks of: “I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls”.

Likewise, we are going to have to do the same thing for our brothers and our sisters. We have to become their sacrifice. Many don't pay attention to this: when they put you to death out here, the Lord looks at it as a sacrifice. That is why it is said that in Babylon they see your altar. What did they do on the altar? Offer blood sacrifice. They are going to put us to death out here, and that is what the altar represents.

We are unto God “a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish”. The ones who walk the other way are the ones who “in time past” walked “according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience”. Those children of disobedience are in the churches, in the mosques, in everything, thinking that is the way. Satan works in them because they keep no commandment. The way is through God's law, statutes and commandments, to his son Jesus the Christ.

So walking in love is walking as Christ walked: keeping the commandments, and giving ourselves for our people as he gave himself, an offering the Lord receives as a sweetsmelling savour.

precepts.label: Leviticus 26:36-37
precepts.why:
This is where the breaking of “the pride of your power” leads. “And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies”. Into their minds: mentally and spiritually, you are going to be broken down. Then “the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them”: no courage. And “they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.”

“And they shall fall one upon another, as it were before a sword, when none pursueth: and ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies.” Think about that spiritually. Take 2026. When black people get mad at other black people, do we show each other mercy, or do we go full-fledged? We even came up with terms for it: turning up, going savage, crashing out. But do we have that same level of aggression toward white police, or the other nations, or the Chinese? Not at all. We will stand and be aggressive with each other all day long, cuss each other out, beat each other up, kill each other. But we will not stand before the other nations. And to be clear, we do not advocate violence on anybody. The point is that the spirit is not the same toward the nations as it is toward each other.

That faintness is on the face of the African brother who said the colonizers left too early, that we are not prepared to rule ourselves. Not only defeated but subdued: low self-esteem, lack of confidence, self-hate, no faith in his own people. It is seen in a whole country left to itself that looks to the white man, to foreign aid and loans, to save it: a mall built under Chinese direction with not a brick out of place, while what our people build for ourselves has uneven steps and lopsided houses. You can’t do nothing right for yourself. That is what comes of low self-esteem.

So this is the fruit of verse 17, “they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you”, and of verse 19, the pride of our power broken. These are the minds the Lord is going to use our brothers to change.

precepts.label: James 2:1
precepts.why:
Moses charged the judges: “Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great”. You shall not have respect of persons in judgment; you cannot be partial. You have to hear both sides, the small as well as the great. That is the qualification of a judge, and if you are not ready for it, do not accept the position.

James speaks of the same thing: “My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.” Here is respect of persons, and James sets it against the faith of Christ itself. You cannot hold the faith of the Lord of glory and at the same time judge one brother by a different measure than another.

“ye shall not be afraid of the face of man”. You are not here to be loved or to be liked; you are judges. Some are afraid to make a decision because of what men will think of them, and some get offended when judgment falls on their friend, even without knowing what happened. What does that have to do with you? The judgment is God's, and a judge in Israel must be just, not partial.

precepts.label: James 2:4
precepts.why:
“Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” Respect of persons goes into having a certain type of man in admiration over another: respecting one over another, preferring one over another, and it shows in how you deal with matters with that brother or those brothers. You are ready to have men's persons in admiration for advantage; there is something you are going to gain by showing favoritism.

And here is the end result: you “are become judges of evil thoughts”. Some brothers are horrible judges because there is something about the person they should judge that they can gain from them. Whether he gives you gifts, whether he is your ride to Sabbath, whether he got you a job, whatever the case may be, now you are partial in your judgment because of what that person can provide for you. The Lord says that is an evil, evil thing.

So you might think, I am just not going to judge because that is my friend. The Bible says you are evil. That is exactly what Moses forbade when he charged the judges to “judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.”

precepts.label: James 2:9
precepts.why:
“But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.” We always hear thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steal; we know those like the back of our hand. But if you have respect of persons, whether in judgment or in having men's persons in admiration for advantage, you commit sin. You are a transgressor, breaking the commandments of God.

You want to be in that position, but much is required of you in the position as judges. You must judge matters and deal righteously, because that is the law of God we just read in Deuteronomy: judge righteous judgment, whether it is your friend or not. In a position of leadership you cannot conceal your friend's folly; none of us should.

What has been discovered is that because someone is your friend, you do not want to speak out. You do not want to reveal the sin, as Leviticus 5:1 requires, and you do not want to be part of the judgment once the sin is revealed. You sit there quiet while the others bring out the transgressions, because you do not agree with the judgment God says to bring forth. Something is wrong with that. We have to stand on what God said. Anyone you consider a friend who goes against God and does not repent: I never knew you. Give us a little time and we will not even remember his name, because he chose wickedness and evil over the righteousness of God.

thread.label: Deuteronomy 7:6-10
thread.text: For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

classes.title: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.label: Leviticus 20:26
precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself”. He chose you to be special unto him, set apart from everybody else. So the question is: what makes us holy? What scripture?

Leviticus 20:26 was brought from the floor as the answer: “And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.” The Lord is holy, and he severed Israel from other people to be his. That severing is the same set-apart people of Deuteronomy 7:6, chosen “above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

So there has to be something we are doing that makes us different. We cannot be doing the same thing the world is doing, and we cannot be doing what the churches are doing. What severs us from the other people is the laws of God being applied, which is what Romans 7:12 goes on to show.

precepts.label: Romans 7:12
precepts.why:
“Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” If the law is holy, and God says you are a holy people, then we are supposed to be a law-abiding people. The laws of God are our constitution, the thing we stand on. That is what makes us holy, what makes us special, what makes us set apart: the laws being applied.

The word of God has no power unless you activate it, and the only way to activate it is to do what it says to do. Other than that it is just pages, just words on a page, just a book. The word is alive and living when you let it live through you by your actions. You become the word, the living example of what it means to be a holy people. That is why the nations say, what a wise and understanding people. They see our actions.

We witness that already at the big events in the big arenas. They say, thousands of black men and nobody smoking weed, no fights breaking out. Then look at what happened in Houston at the rodeo, and how they laughed at us; we are a joke to them. But when we move they ask, how are they so organized, how can they mobilize a few thousand men, put them on the street and file them back in like that, nobody fighting and the place clean? That is the word of God working through us. There is a standard we live by because we are gods on the earth, and it is second nature to us as a nation.

So do not walk in hypocrisy. God gave us something that will make us shine bright and obtain the kingdom. Be that living example to the people.

precepts.label: Matthew 9:36
precepts.why:
“But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.” As Christ went out teaching, healing and doing miracles, he looked and saw that his people fainted. They were out in the streets, they did not worship their God, and their own leaders were taking advantage of them at that time.

It is the same in this captivity as in the time of Rome. Look at our people out there: they are lost, they have no shepherd, they are confused. Not only have the people of the world taken advantage of us, but our own people take advantage too, using the knowledge to get preeminence.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 15:3
precepts.why:
What is going on in 1 Samuel 15? The Lord commanded Saul to utterly destroy all the Amalekites and everything they have, every last one of them. The Lord told Saul, wipe these devils out. And he didn’t do it.

The commandment was total: “Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.” All that they have. All means everything.

Now hold that against Saul’s answer in verse 20: “Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord, and have gone the way which the Lord sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.” Wait a minute: the king is still alive. What do you mean you followed the commandment of the Lord? Saul is playing the defensive, justifying himself, making excuses.

Then verse 21: “But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God in Gilgal.” It wasn’t me, it was the people, it was their fault; I couldn’t do nothing about it. That is bashfulness: you don’t take accountability. The commandment said spare the sheep and oxen not, and Saul brought them back and blamed the people.

So Samuel answered, “to obey is better than sacrifice.” To do what you were told is better than coming back saying, my bad, I thought I understood what you wanted, I decided to do it this way. You fulfill the commandment you were given, and if there is a problem, you say something.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 15:28
precepts.why:
Saul finally confessed in verse 24: “I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.” If you are a leader and you are in fear of your people, or you don’t want them to be mad at you, what can those people do to you? Manipulate you. You are a pushover; they can sway you to the left and to the right. Who is supposed to move you? The Lord, not the people you are supposed to lead. You are not leading the people; you are being led by the people.

Then verse 28: “And Samuel said unto him, The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou.” Damn.

That is what the bashful spirit costs. Verse 23 already said it: “Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.” When you are in that spirit the Lord can’t use you; you are not a good leader. Leadership may see something in you and put you in a position, and then when we question you on certain things you make excuses, or you separate yourself into a bubble with the men under you. You are bashful, you are bringing up a bunch of bashful brothers under you, and you are keeping the brothers under you hostage.

The Lord had made Saul king “When thou wast little in thine own sight”, when he thought he was a nobody. And because he feared the people and would not obey, the kingdom was torn from him and given to his neighbour, David, who was better than he.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 10:2
precepts.why:
“And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” He was scared. This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, what is that going to do to the soldiers under him? It is going to spread.

“As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers”: so are they that are under him. “And what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” Whatever man the ruler is, like King Saul, such are all that dwell under him.

Take an example. Some brothers have been here six months, a year maybe, not long, still in regular clothes. Some officers have been here eight, nine, ten years. Those young men in the regular shirts are going to follow the example of the officers in the purple shirts. So if you are bashful, afraid, timid and shy, what does that communicate to them spiritually? That they can be timid, shy, fearful and bashful too. You don’t have to say nothing; your spirit is telling them, it’s okay to be like this, the officer can be fearful and timid, so I’ll follow his example, now I know how to move around in here.

It shall not be so. It shall not be so in here.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 17:12
precepts.why:
Saul saw the host of the Philistines and “was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” What is fear? “For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.”

A soldier broke it down: the succours go into comfort, and fear betrays that comfort. What reason offers is the lies you make up in your head. You trick yourself into being scared, because you make up things in your mind which ain’t really there.

And on top of that, fear is a lack of faith. Your faith is supposed to be in the Lord, but a lot of the time your faith is basically what you can see with your eyes. Saul looked at the host of the Philistines with his eyes and his heart trembled, instead of trusting the Lord who had made him king.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 5:7
precepts.why:
“For we walk by faith, not by sight.” Christians use that all the time and don’t know what it means. But in this aspect we can use it about fear.

We fear what we see. We don’t fear the Lord; we fear what we physically see. A brother at camp gets unruly with us, he’s got a gun or a knife or whatever, and we fear that. But we don’t fear breaking God’s commandments. That we don’t really fear.

That was Saul. When he “saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid.” He walked by sight. He feared the Philistines he could see and the people who were scattering from him, but he did not fear transgressing the commandment of the Lord, and it cost him the kingdom.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 1:7-8
precepts.why:
“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear.” The Bible says the Lord never gave us that spirit. So the fear Saul had when his heart greatly trembled goes back into a lack of faith.

“But of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” We are supposed to have the spirit of power, love and a sound mind.

“Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God.” We are not supposed to be ashamed of the testimony of Christ. The bashful brother is ashamed and afraid; the one who has God’s spirit partakes of the afflictions of the gospel by the power of God.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:28
precepts.why:
“And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul.” This is the level we have to get to: where we are not afraid of those brothers and sisters, and the other nations, that can kill the body and have power over us in this society.

“But rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” That is the Lord. We need to fear the Lord, the one who can kill body and soul in hell.

Saul feared the Philistines and feared the people, and not the Lord. So, back to 1 Samuel 28:6: “when Saul enquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.” The Lord was not dealing with Saul anymore. He went to the witch at Endor, the same kind he had put out of the land, and Samuel told him, “the Lord is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy.” Because he was bashful, self-willed, easily manipulated and made excuses, he lost the kingdom. Fear the Most High, not man.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 18:10-11
precepts.why:
This is the commandment Saul turned around and broke: “There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits.” The Lord said none of these would be found among Israel.

Saul had just rid the land of all of them: the soothsayers, the witches, the familiar spirits and the wizards. That is what the woman at En-dor throws back at him: “thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?” You trying to get me killed.

Now the Lord has stopped answering him, “neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets”, and the same man who cut them off says, “Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her.” Find me a wizard so I can know what is going on. His mind is all over the place. He is double-minded, breaking the very commandment he had enforced, and he disguises himself and goes by night so no one will see it.

That is where bashfulness leads: self-willed, disobedient, deceitful, making excuses, easily manipulated. Samuel tells him the Lord “is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy.” The Lord rent the kingdom out of his hand and gave it to David, and Saul and his sons would be with Samuel the next day. “There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness.” Saul never believed in himself, so he never believed God; he had Samuel's counsel the whole time and would not listen, and when that guidance was gone he ran to the very thing the law forbade.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 11:16
precepts.why:
“So built we the wall”: all through our history, the forefathers were building. What we are doing today is nothing different from what they always did, and Ezekiel shows the kind of building the Lord gives us while we are scattered.

“Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.” Israel was cast far off and scattered, and the Lord still gave them little sanctuaries in the lands where they came.

When Paul went to Galatia, to Colossae, to Corinth and to Thessalonica, those were sanctuaries, just like the ones you see today. The schools are those little sanctuaries in the countries, and each and every one of us put a hand into building each and every one of them.

So the wall of Nehemiah and the little sanctuary of Ezekiel are the same work. The people built because they had a mind to work, and that mind to work is what leadership has to put into the people now.

precepts.label: Matthew 6:22
precepts.why:
The people built the wall because they “had a mind to work.” This is how a leader’s mindset must be, and Christ shows it: “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.”

A single eye is being locked in, what they call laser focus. Whatever you are locked in on, that is what you are going to see. That is all you are going to see, and that is all that matters.

And when the leader is like that, guess who else is going to be like that? Everybody underneath him. The single eye of the one at the head fills the whole body with light, so the whole camp takes on his focus.

That is why the wall got built. The mind to work in the people starts with the mind of the one leading them.

Everything rises and falls on leadership. There are cities where the leader was changed and the camp took off, and other places where the leader left and everything fell apart. “Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.” When a brother falls, you have to build and restore this man back to life. “Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.” If we were in that same situation, we would want our brothers to come and get us out of it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 6:8
precepts.why:
Job 33:23 speaks of “a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand”. You are the interpreter, brother, and you are that one among a thousand. When you are one among a thousand, that makes you a leader, and you have to have the mind of a leader. Any place you step into, your mindset shouldn't be to fit in; you should be figuring out how to make it better. Joseph didn't go into Egypt and just sit there; he asked how we are going to solve the problem. The Lord gave us wisdom, discretion, judgment and skill sets.

The first thing in the mindset of a leader is that he believes he can get the job done. That is what separates you from everybody else. When an issue arises, you don't run. You raise your hand, you volunteer, you figure out a solution to the problem.

Isaiah shows it: “Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Who is going to go on our behalf? “Then said I, Here am I; send me.” That's the mindset of a leader.

That is the same thing David did. Everybody kept crying about the situation, and David said, where is Goliath at? Show me. The first thing you have to have is a willingness and a belief in completing the task, whatever it may be, and that mindset alone sets you apart. That is what the Lord has put in your spirit to do: not an unsure mind that says maybe I can, but send me.

precepts.label: Psalms 55:21
precepts.why:
“For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it.” It was not the enemy that set David up, or he would have been ready, because he knows who the enemy is. “But it was thou, a man mine equal, my guide, and mine acquaintance. We took sweet counsel together, and walked unto the house of God in company.” It was the man he trusted, the man he went fishing with, and that took him by surprise. Later in the same psalm David describes that man: “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.”

A man mine equal: an officer of ten, of twenty, of fifty, just like me. We took sweet counsel together: Deacon, I need counsel; Captain, what do you think about this? But while he was taking counsel, he was plotting. Some are plotting to take your wife: she is too beautiful for him. Some are plotting to take your position at the job you brought them into, telling the white man, give me his position. I picked him up every Sabbath and every Wednesday, and when he came to betray me he had no problem doing it.

“Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.” Christ was betrayed that way: “Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?” Today we do not kiss, but we dap: Shalom, Captain, Most High bless. That smooth greeting can be the betrayal. In 2018 a man who sat in another man's house, barbecued and travelled with him, came and took all his furniture and put his children to sleep on the cold floor.

Jeremiah warns: “Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.” Supplant means betray, plot. Other camps slander our members and leadership, because they know our people believe anything without proof; they are Esau in black skin, who “have taught their tongue to speak lies.” They come asking to fellowship, but we are not stupid.

It was not the enemy that killed Thomas Sankara; it was his best friend, who grew up with him. It was Maduro's own handpicked bodyguards who stood down and handed him over, taking American money instead of a bullet for him. That is war in the heart behind smooth words. David is telling you: do not fall asleep.

precepts.label: Psalms 58:3
precepts.why:
“He hath put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him: he hath broken his covenant.” Venezuela is a peaceful country. America put an embargo and sanctions on Venezuela for twenty years to destroy its economy; the money goes down, everything goes down. Then twenty years later: he is a drug dealer, he is this, he is that; people of Venezuela, we can change your lives. America did that. “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart.”

Only the simple will believe it was about drug trafficking. Trump pardoned one of the biggest drug dealers a couple of months before, and Mexico, on America's border, has more drug cartels than any place in the world. Then the story shifted to oil. They use the same stupidity because they know some black people will believe that garbage. Ninety-nine point nine percent of the words that come out of the Trump mouth are a lie. He lies even when he is not talking; he is blinking and lying, and every person who works for him too.

David shows why: “The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies.” The little baby is born, he does not even talk yet, and he is looking at you lying. That is Trump: before he can say a word he already starts lying. All of them. God said it, not me: it is in them to be liars. And our people believe them, because they are white. Who told you the white man cannot lie?

Habakkuk describes the same man, whose “soul which is lifted up is not upright in him.” Esau is not right: “he is a proud man, neither keepeth at home”: he is in everybody's business, with bases around the world used to overthrow any government that does not do what he says. He destroys the economy with sanctions, sends in CIA agitators and propaganda to raise the people up, and then comes back as the good guy offering to help. Like a man who rapes a woman and then offers to take her to therapy.

That is putting forth his hands against such as be at peace with him. The wicked go astray from the womb speaking lies, and his smooth words always have war in his heart.

It is biblically impossible to understand this Bible while you are not observing the laws of God. There is no way around it. That is why Christ's message from the start was this: “From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.”

So many of our brothers and sisters out in the world have yet to come to grips with what we are here for. Being an Israelite in Christ is not about dressing up as an Israelite. It's not about arguing with white folks in the streets. It's not about flexing your muscles and trying to be a tough guy. And no, it is not about multiple wives.

Being an Israelite in Christ is about observing the Most High God's commandments and faith in his Son, so that we don't die when the Lord returns. The kingdom of heaven is at hand, and you are at risk if you do not repent and seek the kingdom. Point blank, period.

Those who deny Christ and deny keeping the commandments, because they want to fulfil their own lust, come up with absurd breakdowns of scripture. Without repentance there is no good understanding.

precepts.why:
Wisdom says, “Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness. My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold.” What are those riches? Colossians shows it: “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.”

The riches we are looking for are not money, though people think they are. We need the durable riches, which is wisdom: the word of Christ dwelling in us richly. And this is what we are supposed to do with it: teach and admonish one another.

God says, I am giving it to you. But you are walking in hypocrisy, distracted by covetousness, and a man’s life does not consist of the abundance of what he has. That was not their kingdom at that point, and all of this is coming to an end anyway. God has something far better than what you are looking at, and you are about to throw it away for this world.

Now you understand what the scripture is saying, so you have no excuse. Much is given, so much is required, and the one who knew will be beaten with many stripes. So I have to walk in that, stand in that space and be that, or get ready to get beat. The durable riches of Proverbs 8 are the word living in us richly, and they have to be walked in.

precepts.label: Romans 6:1
precepts.why:
The question put to the class: you're alone online late at night, temptation hits, and nobody from the congregation would know. What shows integrity? A, entertain the temptation privately. B, watch a little and justify it later. C, cut it off immediately and fight temptation. D, convince yourself grace covers everything. Answer D is a scary mindset to have, and Paul already answered it: “What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?”

Shall we continue in sin that grace may cover everything? That is a terrible mindset, and it is the mindset of Christianity: I found grace, grace covers me, I can do what I want when I want. All I have to do is believe in Jesus; I ain't got to do nothing he says, just believe he's my Lord and savior. Christianity is evil.

The answer is C. The questions are easy and the answers are easy; the problem is when it comes to fruition in real time. You are fighting your war against yourself: you don't want to push play, but you want to push play, and nobody is there to tell you a damn thing. That is when C gets blurred out.

The real battlefield is private. A lot of people fall spiritually in secret long before they fall publicly. The representative shows up at the Sabbath; the real you shows up at home, alone, with your family, and your wife knows exactly who you are. You can't salute so hard you're over righteous and then go home and verbally, financially or physically abuse your wife. And sisters, you can't bow 90 degrees at the door and then go home, cuss your husband out, and keep a filthy house. That is lacking integrity and poor character.

That is Proverbs 11:3: “The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.” Grace is not a cover for sin; integrity is acting on what you know, even when nobody is watching.

precepts.why:
“The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way: but the folly of fools is deceit.” The fool deceives himself and ignores the red flags. One of the plainest is trust in place of proof. Bishop Yawsaw told of a situation, and it is happening all over the nation: a sister was asked, Did y’all show each other your STD test results? She said, I trust him.

“Thus saith the Lord; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm.” Miss me with the trust. I trust God. When you make flesh your arm, you make another human being your strength, the one you rely on and believe in. No: I need to see the test.

It is a red flag if someone does not want to go get tested. What do you have to hide? What are you scared of? If you have not been doing anything, you have nothing to hide; but if you are nasty, now you are scared and running from the truth. Six or seven months of excuses, I had to work, something happened with my insurance, and then you wake up with the love bump, because you were so worried about laying down with the sister that you did not care that she never took the test.

In this present world there need to be multiple tests, and you have to go to the hospital with them, because people are sending someone else in or having AI make them an STD chart, and you think it is official. That is the prudent man understanding his way. The sister who says I trust him has made flesh her arm, and the scripture says that trust is cursed.

Your pastors could have been the negroes in the world, leaders who just seek after covetousness. But the Lord led you to pastors according to his heart, brothers who are able to help you build and help you see yourself. They feed you with knowledge and understanding, so that is who you seek after.

That isn't hurting somebody else; you are destroying your own soul, because you can't be corrected, which means you can't grow. This is why: “A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool.”

As a foolish person, you cannot allow wisdom to enter in. You're sitting around the men, you're in the school with all these men, you see everybody growing around you, and for some reason you know everything, but the wisdom can't take hold and exalt you the way it exalts all the rest who take hold of it. You're fighting against it.

That is why some have been in the truth 10 or 15 years and are still a soldier. How long you been with us? 10 years. What's your rank? Officer of 10, sir. Why? I don't know, sir. You know. You know everything else but that. You can't say you've been held back. Ten years and you're only able to deal with ten men: that is a problem.

That is when it is time to take stock in yourself, and a lot of people don't want to do that, because they don't want the integrity that comes with the Bible. The one who hears reproof gets understanding; the fool takes a hundred stripes and learns nothing.

Sisters, these are the things to look for. You see the signs. You hear it in his speech and in his daily decision-making. He doesn't know if he is coming or going: one minute it's this, the next minute it's that. He has something brand new he is trying to bring out, like mashed potatoes on the Passover, and you know it did not come from leadership. Red flag. And when he fixes it, sister, you better run.

This is the man you are going to hop behind and expect to make sure everything is taken care of? You mess around and be homeless, trying to figure it out. He is not ready yet. He is unstable.

So when looking for a husband, ask: does this man have stability, does he have discipline? A man with no rule over his spirit is not mentally sound, and he cannot take care of you. Aim up, never down: look for a man with more understanding than you, who can lead you and guide you.

“Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.” The last part is the point: the kisses of an enemy are deceitful. And Luke shows the kiss: “Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?” Judas betrayed Christ with a kiss. The man betrayed him with the very sign of love.

Today we do not greet each other with a kiss like that, but we have our own greeting: Shalom, Captain, Most High bless. That is the betrayal. The embrace, the salute, the Shalom, and then the knife. That is the kiss of an enemy.

We saw it in 2018. A man who had been in another man’s house, greeting him with Shalom, barbecuing together, traveling together, came to that same man’s house, took all his furniture and put his children on the cold floor to sleep. He did not care. Not only did he betray the man, he betrayed all his children.

There is nothing worse than a traitor. And some of you think once you betray your brother or your sister, that is the end of it. It is not. The one who betrays with a kiss will be dealt with too. That is why the kisses of an enemy are called deceitful: Judas is the pattern of the familiar hand that destroys.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 6:10
precepts.why:
“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. What is the thing that hath been? Solomon says: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man”. So the thing is man.

Read Ecclesiastes 1:9 again with that: “and that which is done is that which shall be done”. The same thing man did in the past, he is going to come back and do again. “there is no new thing under the sun.” If you were wicked in the past, you are going to be wicked again when you come back on the earth. That is why the scripture says he that is righteous, let him be righteous still, and he that is evil, let him be evil still. If you are righteous, you will gravitate to righteous brothers and sisters; if you are wicked, to wicked people.

Why is this important? Because what was done to us in slavery is a circle coming back around. God's judgment is as a ring. Slavery isn't over; the white man put a fake smile on his face, and now he is showing his real face. It is the same people coming back to do the same thing. Antiochus died long ago under the Greeks, yet the scripture says he shall stand up against the Prince of princes, because the same spirit that came against the holy people is going to do it again.

So just as Egypt said, the children of Israel “are more and mightier than we”, and “let us deal wisely with them”, America, spiritual Egypt, does the same today: the census, abortions and Planned Parenthood, changing laws as we become the majority. The thing that repeats is man himself.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:8
precepts.why:
“The burden of Egypt.” Egypt was before Isaiah’s time, so what Egypt is this speaking about? Revelation answers it: “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

It says spiritually. Sodom is not around anymore; it is destroyed, those cities of Sodom and Gomorrah near Ein Bokek are nothing. But spiritual Sodom is here. It goes on even in the landmass of Israel among the Israelis, but prominently and predominately here in America, with all types of switcheroos: men acting like women and women acting like men, committing things contrary to the laws of God. And it is spiritual Egypt, the house of bondage. So replace Egypt with America: the burden of America.

“where also our Lord was crucified.” They crucify Christ in his image, in his message, and in denying that you men are the greatest thing on the face of this earth. They say, hell no, all people, God loves everybody.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city.” America is that great city, and our people are spiritually dead here. They are fearful of freedom; there is no spirit in them to rebel with the laws of God.

So when Isaiah says the Lord rides upon a swift cloud and comes into Egypt, it is the Lord coming with his chariots and angels to bring wrath and destruction upon America. Its idols shall be moved at his presence, and its heart, the mindset, doctrines and mentality of the oppressive kingdom, shall melt in the midst of it. He will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: militia against militia, civil war, brother against brother, city against city. This place is divided; the stars are falling and the stripes are broken. That is Esau rising against himself, and it is not our fight.

precepts.label: Jude 1:20-21
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the Lord keeps him in perfect peace “because he trusteth in thee.” That is the key part. You trust in the Lord, you trust in his words, and you build yourself up. Jude says it: “But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost”.

It is the leaders' job to build the man, but once you have the foundation, it is on you to take the notes from the classes, apply them to yourself and add to them. Do a serious checkup from the neck up. Take an erasable dry marker to your mirror and write your issues with the scriptures next to them, what you need to fix, and at the top write: execute. Those are your orders for the day. If you don't see it, you're never going to fix it. Too many brothers and sisters don't write anything down: notes done, Bible closed the rest of the week, and then they're stressing, when the fix to what they were dealing with last week and what they will face this week came out in the class. We don't examine ourselves.

Don't ask the captain what he sees in you. What do you see in you? Leadership has the blessing of discernment, but that only goes so far; we can't see through you or know all the deep recesses of what you're dealing with. You have to go before the Lord, explain it, confess it, and ask him in sincerity to remove those things from you.

Don't play with what you know you are dealing with. The spirits on brothers and sisters who could care less can rub off even on leadership; a lot of brothers and sisters are spiritual vampires, and it takes a toll on leaders who love our people. God has this hospital set up for you to get the help, and the medicine is the laws. You have a headache, you don't throw the Tylenol in the trash, you take it. So why throw away the medicine when it concerns your soul and your salvation? Why be fearful of freedom?

“Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life.” Keep yourselves in the love of God, not in the crosshairs of his anger, his rage, his wrath. It is our job to keep ourselves there. I can't save you, and you can't save me. It ain't going to be easy; you have to go through this fiery trial to get the kingdom. So do your part. You have the keys to freedom, and that is the trust that keeps the mind stayed on the Lord in perfect peace.

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
What actually brings us peace? Not enlisting in this war, and not hoping America goes back to the old ways. “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee”. The mind that is stayed on the Lord is the mindset of Joshua 1:8: the book of the law does not depart out of your mouth, and you meditate on it day and night.

That is your four chapters a day. That is you not separating yourself, and having that godly conversation consistently, as in Malachi, where they thought upon the Lord's name and a book of remembrance was written. That is making sure the sick among us in the congregations are well taken care of. That is you men doing the blitz, traveling, doing your due diligence by all manner to get out of that black shirt and get out here and teach your people, to become men of valor and soldiers of the Lord, and put in your brick.

You establish yourself on the laws of God. That is your meditation, your chief joy. You're not worried about what is played on the radio, and you could give a damn about what's on the internet unless it is funneled through the Bible so you can keep up with the times.

Then the news, the destruction and the chaos won't worry you. You'll have a Coke bottle smile from one ear to the next, because you know the mysteries. You're not fearful of freedom. The mind that meditates on the law day and night is the mind the Lord keeps in perfect peace.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 30:16
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls Israel “a people robbed and spoiled.” We are robbed of our nationality, robbed of the understanding that we are the twelve tribes of the children of Israel. Jeremiah shows how we are spoiled, and what the Lord will do about it.

“Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured”: that is going to take place upon the oppressors of our people. “and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity”: the adversaries are all the nations outside of the children of Israel, and every one of the nations that oppress us shall go into captivity.

How do they spoil us? Over a multitude of captivities the children of Israel have gone into, every single nation has had its hand in the oppression of the twelve tribes. That includes the Arabs, that a lot of brothers and sisters want to cry over when they see what is going on in Palestine. Those people had our people oppressed too; they were spoiling the hell out of us. What we are seeing overseas right now is the righteous judgment of the Lord, prophecy fulfilling right now.

Yet brothers and sisters are so damn fearful to escape this captivity and get themselves together, even as the prophecies come to pass. Many are called, but few are chosen, so self-examine. With bombs dropping and rumors of war, men are still catting around, committing fornication, letting their wives rule over them and hide their folly, paying for prostitutes, hooked on marijuana and controlled by the porn system. Our people are sick; they are afraid of freedom, because sin controls them.

“and they that spoil thee shall be a spoil, and all that prey upon thee will I give for a prey.” The nations that spoiled us shall in turn be a spoil for us, because the tables are turned. We serve a just God. So Isaiah’s people “for a prey” and “for a spoil” will not stay that way: those that prey upon Israel are given for a prey themselves.

Our job is not to pick up guns and knives thinking you can do something to the white man; this man will wipe you out just like that. “come, and let us declare in Zion the work of the Lord our God.” We are Zion, and our job is to declare in Zion the work of the Lord: what is coming, and how to fix your spirit and build yourself up. To our brothers and sisters in Venezuela: repent. You cannot stop the white man; let him do what he was supposed to do. The evil in the city is the Lord’s counsel standing, and it is revealed to his prophets.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:1-6
precepts.why:
We say give the Lord no rest, make the time short, bring it on: when is he coming to get us out? We are trying to speed the Lord up. But the Lord has his timetable and a reason for the pace he is moving at, and when it is time for him to move, you can't stop it. Esau won't be able to stop it. “Therefore shall evil come upon thee; thou shalt not know from whence it riseth: and mischief shall fall upon thee; thou shalt not be able to put it off.” When all the planets have lined up, it is time to send Christ and the destroying angels to bring his people home, and if you are not ready, he comes as a thief in the night.

Ezra shows the mind of the Most High, his vantage point: “Before the fair flowers were seen, or ever the moveable powers were established, before the innumerable multitude of angels were gathered together, Or ever the heights of the air were lifted up, before the measures of the firmament were named, or ever the chimneys in Sion were hot” … “before they were sealed that have gathered faith for a treasure.”

“Then did I consider these things, and they all were made through me alone, and through none other: by me also they shall be ended, and by none other.” The Most High made all of that, so we can't question that kind of understanding. We are not on the level to question how the Lord did things. Nobody did this but him, and by him alone it shall be ended.

So he sends Christ when he is ready to send Christ. We don't know the day or the hour, but we know we are in the season, and the enemies of the Lord include some of our own people siding with the oppressors by agreeing to be in sin and destroying their own people. That is not the agencies; that is negroes being wicked as hell, and negro is a mind state across all twelve tribes that was never supposed to be you. Knowing these things are coming, we need to get our minds and our spirits right.

precepts.label: Isaiah 40:13-17
precepts.why:
God's vantage point is far beyond the vantage point we think we have. People try to tell the Lord what to do: you can't love Jacob, you can't hate Esau, you can't forgive this one. So the Lord clears the deck and lets everybody know where he stands, and everybody else needs to shut the hell up.

“Who hath directed the Spirit of the Lord, or being his counsellor hath taught him?” Nobody. These are questions for us who are trying to push him. The dumb Christian talks about the way the Lord should be; shut up. “With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of judgment, and taught him knowledge, and shewed to him the way of understanding?” Who taught God knowledge? Nobody. God is the knowledge; how are you going to teach him?

Having asked questions we can't answer, he proclaims what it is: “Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket.” You walk with a pail of water and one drop falls out; you won't even notice it. All the nations put together are that one drop. They “are counted as the small dust of the balance”: not big dust, small dust on the scales, weighing nothing. “He taketh up the isles as a very little thing”: the Polynesian and Hawaiian islands, very little, nothing.

“And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering.” If they burnt up all the meat in Lebanon, it would not be sufficient for him to accept the Arabs, Ishmael, as his people. Only the Israelites are his people; that is why the first verse of the chapter says, comfort ye my people.

“All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.” Less than nothing is spit, a bowel movement. That is how the nations are counted to God, while to us he says comfort ye my people. That is the difference, and nobody can say anything against it. 2 Esdras 6:55-56 parallels it and calls them spittle: Ezra was quoting Isaiah. The supreme power has it set up the way he wants it set up.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:16
precepts.why:
“The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted.” He has chosen and set apart every man here, all the captains, to preach good tidings to the meek. But how do you bind up a person that is broken? The brokenhearted are broken in the mind: suffering the curses without knowing the will of God. We are set apart to bind them up. What do we bind them with?

“Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” We bind up the testimony and seal the law in the minds of the people, because they are brokenhearted and their minds are broken. That is what we are called to do: to bind them to the laws of God.

And we show them why it is good. Look at our lives as the example of what it means to serve God and why it is good to serve him. That means we have to be sincere about it. How do we tell the people to touch not the unclean thing and then not live it ourselves? The one who was profitable to many but not to himself will be punished accordingly, because he knew better.

So the good tidings we proclaim with the law are these: if we repent and keep God's laws in sincerity and endure to the end, he will deliver us, and we will rule again, as we were made in his image to rule.

precepts.label: Isaiah 49:1-8
precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 says to “proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord”, and Isaiah 49 says it again: “Thus saith the Lord, In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee: and I will preserve thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages.” The acceptable year and the acceptable time: that is when we heal the broken heart and proclaim liberty to the captives.

“The Lord hath called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name. And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me, and made me a polished shaft; in his quiver hath he hid me; And said unto me, Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified.” We are supposed to glorify our God in this body.

“Then I said, I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain: yet surely my judgment is with the Lord, and my work with my God.” We go to stiff-necked, hard-hearted people who refuse to hear the word of God, but we still proclaim the day of the Lord to heal those minds and tell them there is an end to this: we will rule one day. He formed us from the womb “to bring Jacob again to him.”

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” It may not appear that we are doing it, but when the numbers come in, it is a light thing he has given us, and he still charges us to raise up the children of Israel. “I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth”: that goes back to Matthew 4, the Gentiles of Galilee. Our job is to bring salvation to the people and lead them back to him, and that is a great ministry.

“Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship” … “and he shall choose thee.” Out of all of them, he is going to choose us. And unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: we want to be the faithful servant the Lord finds doing this work in sincerity, without deceit and without secret sins.

precepts.label: Haggai 1:4
precepts.why:
The Lord told Jeremiah, “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” God sent Jeremiah with a purpose. But Jeremiah felt he was too young, that it was not the time: “Ah, Lord God! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child.”

Some of us think the same way, that now is not the time. That is what Haggai answered: is it time for you to dwell in your ceiled houses, and the house of the Lord lie waste? Now is not the time to build your own house first. What about the house of the Lord?

The Lord did not accept Jeremiah's excuse: “Say not, I am a child: for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak.” That is a commandment. precepts.why:
“Blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord, and whose hope the Lord is. For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, and that spreadeth out her roots by the river”. The one who trusts in the Lord and makes the Lord his hope, the Lord nourishes. A little plant next to a river never lacks water. When the heat comes the sun may be hot, but you will not feel it, because the hand of God covers you up. “but her leaf shall be green”: you stay green, you stay with wisdom.

Solomon shows what staying green looks like in a sister: “She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.” That is a sister who stays in the green, the little plant by the water. When she opens her mouth, she opens it with wisdom, like someone who has understanding.

When that verse is not fulfilled in your house, that is why the house is not blessed. You wonder why you and your husband are going through things; that verse is not being fulfilled in that house.

The same goes for how we take correction. Asking to explain yourself after admitting to every charge is of the devil; Satan will make you look stupid, and it is better to just listen. The correction given is good for the one who gives it and the one who receives it. That knife cuts both ways: it cuts the one corrected, and the brother correcting says, I have to get my own thing together too. So do not be angry when a brother or sister checks you. Stay by the water and keep your leaf green.

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:2
precepts.why:
“The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?” The heart is the mind, and nothing is more deceitful than the mind. Christ showed what comes out of it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”

Yet Solomon says, “All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes”. Every one of us thinks we are righteous. Ask them: me? I ain't do nothing. Covetous spirit? Hatred? Oh, no. Judas would have said the same. All our ways are clean in our own eyes.

“but the Lord weigheth the spirits.” The Lord sees everything, and you cannot hide from the Most High. You can fool the deacon, you can fool the bishop and the leadership, but the Most High sees you, and you are not fooling yourself either. You know where you were last night, why you never called the brother back, and why you told her to hush before you answered the phone.

That is Jeremiah 17:10: “I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins”. Only God can search the mind, and he weighs what is really in it, not what we show each other. Read on: “Commit thy works unto the Lord, and thy thoughts shall be established.”

precepts.label: Romans 8:27
precepts.why:
“I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.” Most of us only see each other on the Sabbath, and when we come around each other we are on our best behaviour. Six days a week, Sunday to Friday, we do not know where you are or what you are doing. So what are you doing when you are not here? The sister in Georgia bowed, said shalom and happy Sabbath for ten years while carrying on with the Uber Eats driver. She thought she was fooling us, and surely thought she was fooling the Most High. You cannot fool the Most High.

Paul says the same: “And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit”. The one who searches the heart is searching the mind. And that verse tells you there are two: the spiritual and the physical man. There is a war, the spirit against the flesh, wicked against righteous, darkness against light.

That war will never be over until Christ comes back or you die in this. Some want it to be over and ask why there is so much evil in their head. Maybe because you are not reading enough. Brothers who do not know the scriptures will be the ones to betray you, because when they come to him he will fall. Ask yourself when the brother you talk to during the week last talked scripture with you. The Lord searching the heart gives every man according to his ways: not the deacon's way or the bishop's way, but yours. You are your own biggest enemy.

precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face. Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you”. This is our deliverance from Babylon: we go back into the wilderness, Christ deals with us and teaches us the laws again, and what he is doing to us there is purging.

So what kind of pleading is he going to be doing? Is it baby, baby, please? No. The pleading is killing and smiting, and Isaiah proves it: “For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh”. It's not a damn R&B song.

That is the same fury Ezekiel speaks of: “surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you”. As he pleaded with our fathers in the wilderness of Egypt, where the rebellious fell, he will plead with us, by fire and by the sword.

So even after the deliverance there is still going to be a purge. There will still be bad actors among us, people that still need to get right, and they are going to get it; Christ is the one who will give it to them.

precepts.label: Joel 3:2
precepts.why:
The Lord pleads with the nations the same way he pleads with Israel. Joel says: “I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel”. No baby, baby, please for them either. He will kill them, for his people Israel.

The nations are judged “for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.” The pleading in the valley of Jehoshaphat is the Lord's vengeance on the ones who scattered us.

So when Ezekiel says the Lord will plead with Israel face to face in the wilderness “Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt”, the word means the same thing it means for the nations: judgment, smiting and fire, not begging. He pleads for Israel against the nations, and he pleads with the rebels in Israel in the wilderness, and nobody should read either as the Lord asking nicely.

precepts.label: Matthew 3:12
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “And I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”. What kind of purge is he going to be doing? Killing. Matthew shows it: “Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” Does anybody not understand that?

The wheat is gathered into the garner, and the chaff is burned. That is the rebels who “shall not enter into the land of Israel”. Zechariah is still talking about the purge: “in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.” And even the third that is left still has to be sifted, refined, made right, purged.

The Lord is not going to give the kingdom to wicked negroes. The kingdom will not be open to wicked negroes. To get the kingdom you have to go through this fire and get right; there is no other way. You can't keep doing what you do and think you are going to get the kingdom. It is impossible.

That is why we have to fight for this and help each other. If I see you weak and say nothing to you, that means I hate you. So if I tell you, bro, you have to fix that, and you say I hate you, shut your ass up; I am trying to save your life. We are so used to not taking correction from each other that it feels like hate, because everybody has coddled you, and you keep kicking the can down the street until you are back on the corner doing what you do. The fan is already in his hand.
