precepts.label: Baruch 4:1
precepts.why:
Hosea says of Israel that “they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” Baruch shows what breaking out is: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Such as leave the law, or break away from it, shall die. That is what they break out means.

So the sins Hosea lists, swearing, lying, killing, stealing and committing adultery, are a breaking away from the book of the commandments. Where the law is left, there is no truth, no mercy and no knowledge of God in the land, because truth is the application of God's laws, and the laws of God are not being taught or enforced.

And once they break out, blood toucheth blood: violence, hatred, killing against each other. The law endures for ever and keeping it is life; leaving it is death. The truth is the only thing we have to get up out of here. There is no plan B. Outside of this is death.

That is why the land mourns. If those same sins abide in the body, adultery, stealing, lying, swearing, not applying God's laws, hatred, violence, the congregation will not grow and will not flourish. As leaders we must teach the laws, hold people accountable to them, and be the example ourselves, so people can see there has to be a change in the way we move and how we think.

precepts.label: Amos 3:3
precepts.why:
“Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” That is the answer to the one who decides not to congregate with the body on the Sabbath, or to congregate partially, and then congregates with somebody that has been put out of the body. That is out of order, and it is sin.

The Sabbath is not negotiable: remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. We cannot cook, we cannot buy, we cannot sell on the Lord's Sabbath day, and we must congregate, because it is a holy convocation. There is no way around that; you cannot decide not to do it. It is those small things, the application of God's laws, that separate us.

People do otherwise because we rationalise in our minds what we think is acceptable and what God will be all right with. God said, No, my commandments are straight; this is what I told you to do. Our biggest problem is trying to put our own thoughts in on how it should be done, but the Lord said, Your thoughts are not my thoughts. It is not hard. It only gets hard when we start to rationalise.

Imagine if that is how we started, people coming and going, this one wearing a yarmulke, this one wearing that. That is not how you build God's army. There must be structure, and the leaders are the example, the representative of what a godly Israelite looks like. When there is no agreement in the body, there is no truth in the land, and the land mourns.

Hosea ends with a promise: “he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth.” What is the analogy of the former and latter rain? It's going to be a blessing. When we harvested crops, we looked forward to the rain coming. We needed the rain to come. When it didn't rain, we knew the Lord wasn't dealing with us. That's how he punished us.

We read that in Deuteronomy 28: “And thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass, and the earth that is under thee shall be iron. The Lord shall make the rain of thy land powder and dust: from heaven shall it come down upon thee, until thou be destroyed.” That is what it looks like when the rain does not come: the heaven shut like brass, the ground hard as iron, and powder and dust in place of rain.

So when Hosea says the Lord will come unto us as the rain, it is the curse being lifted. “Come, and let us return unto the Lord: for he hath torn, and he will heal us”. We were torn by captivity and slavery, and he will heal us, meaning redeem us out of this situation. After two days, two thousand years, he revives us, and in the third day he raises us up to who we are, to our identity.

“Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the Lord”: if we follow on to apply what God tells us to do, then shall we be bound up and healed. The rain the Lord withheld in the curses comes back as a blessing, and that blessing will be in the application of his laws.

The Lord answered, “the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come”. “Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world”. How are we poor? Because they robbed us. We have been robbed of our nationality and robbed of our land. Israel is your land: black man, black woman, Latino man, Latino woman, Native American man, Native American woman. We did not know our nationality or our history. But that stops now; now we know.

“Rich in faith”. We are rich because Christ came for us; that is our faith. We keep the commandments and the faith of Jesus Christ, and we have the hope of deliverance coming our way: “heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him”.

That is why we are not fearful of freedom. Every bomb dropped and every war fought is loosening the links of the shackles of our captivity. The Lord is the director of this thing, and those he chose out of poverty are the heirs of the kingdom.

precepts.label: Genesis 34:1-3
precepts.why:
Christ says, “except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.” We claim we want the days shortened, but we are not ready, because wicked brothers are trying to slide in. Brothers and sisters who come from the world with a world mentality would love nothing more than to seduce and defile you, men and women both, because they don't want to change. Negroes don't like change. They pretend they've changed and put on the fringes and the border of blue so you let your guard down, then work behind the scenes to allure you away from your protection.

Dinah shows how it happens, and she was not raped. “And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.” Was she snatched? No, she went out on her own. With a father and twelve mighty brothers, you know they brought her the wisdom that pertains to a woman, and tried to keep her in straitly, the way the scripture says to keep a shameless daughter. She did not want to hear it. She wandered away from her father and her brethren.

“And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.” Something in her spirit let him know. He knew whose daughter she was, and he saw she was not rolling in the spirit of her fathers or her brethren. That is how slick brothers hit sisters in the DMs: they read your spirit when you are not studying, and once they talk that talk, you feed right into it.

“And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.” That is the part that tells you it was not rape: he spake kindly to her. You gave him your ear, he got your underwear. She was enticed, beguiled, allured: drawn away from her protection, from her fathers, from how she was raised, from the protections leadership put around her. Enticing is covetousness; she belonged to Jacob, and he drew her away. Then he asked to marry her, and her brothers said no, you already defiled her. She had to live with that stain for wandering out of her father’s care, and you read nothing of her after that.

Christ warns, “there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect”: some of you men and women of the third slated to make it. Everybody with fringes and a border of blue is not right; do not look at his pretty beard. One who tells women marriage is not the goal and singleness is not the curse, while flaunting his own wife, is the devil in black flesh; he wants the women to stay in sin. A woman in the world turned down one of these street preachers when he broke character to ask for her number. A woman in the world knows more about the commandments than a negro with fringes and a Bible who is supposed to be keeping them, yet a sister in here will entertain the same kind in her DMs. Whoremongering brothers fake the funk, become soldiers, and look for spinsters, sisters anxious about getting older and not married yet, and gas them up, because all bread is sweet to a whoremonger. That is why, when you correctly come together, you exchange medical records and show each other; leadership does not need to see them. Give diligence and study, so you can recognize deception at your door, whatever it is wearing.

Check yourself: maybe talk to the sister who came after you and ask how she did it, instead of calling it hatred from leadership. God put leadership in your life to watch over your soul. Be the Proverbs 31 woman, fix your mouth, do the work on the body, stop eating the ice cream at night, and know your size before you point at the fit brother. The same dumb spirit Christ cast out of the boy tells that sister to go into the world, get a lord, and bring him in, when in the world she caught nothing before. Go into the world and you are still the same negro, still the same woman; you never changed, because you would not go to the Lord. Some came here for the ride and not the work. One sister reached out to a man in the world, and he is gone; another left for a man online who said he did not believe in two or three wives, then found out he did. Some of you are not going to get a lord in this captivity, and if that is what you came for, Satan will move you out of the way.

That spirit is the one that “ofttimes” cast the child “into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him”: the paycheck spent in the club that gets sprayed up, the drunk drive that costs your limbs, the mob on Eastern Parkway, in the mix of a bunch of no-good negroes up to no good. Leaving your house to go with the dumb negroes is a dumb spirit. We thought it was cool; it was a dumb and deaf spirit, not listening and not seeing our condition. “If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth”: your belief is your power. When Satan keeps attacking you, your faith is weak, so cry like the father, “Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.”

“This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.” Some demons are higher than others, so fast and pray, and do not let it conquer you. And once made whole, hear Christ: “sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.” The world you left two years ago is not the world you would go back to; sin has multiplied, and worse demons are jumping on people.

precepts.label: Psalms 119:142
precepts.why:
Hosea prophesied: “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.” These are those days. We were out for a long time, without the understanding of who we were as a people or what the will of God was for us, and in the last days the Lord raised up the prophets on the earth again to teach the word of God and apply it, so we could be delivered out of here. Where in the New Testament do we read that the children of Israel will return and seek the Lord? Right here: “But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him.” That's us, reviving in this time. What you are part of is the resurrection of God's Christ's kingdom, and in that kingdom righteousness must reign. The Father is going to try us to see if we will worship him according to spirit and truth.

And what is the truth? “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” Worshipping in truth is the application of God's laws, the keeping of God's commandments.

“God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.” Emphasise one word: must. There's no other way to do it. Take one law that is not negotiable: remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy. We must congregate, it's a holy convocation; we cannot cook, clean, shop, buy or sell on the Lord's Sabbath. There's no deciding it's not important. It's those small things, the application of God's laws, that separate us. If someone won't congregate with the body and goes to congregate with somebody put out of the body, that's sin: can two walk together except they be agreed? We rationalize in our mind what we think God will be all right with, but his thoughts are not our thoughts. Do what he told you to do.

Where the law is not applied, Hosea says the Lord has a controversy with the land, “because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” There is no knowledge of God because the laws of God are not being taught or enforced. “By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” To break out is to break away from the law: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Blood touching blood is violence and hatred against each other. “Therefore shall the land mourn”: if those same sins abide in the body, the congregation won't grow or flourish. So leaders must teach the laws, hold people accountable to them, and be the example themselves. What God asks is a small thing next to the sins we have committed: not stealing, not swearing, not lying, not committing adultery, keeping the Sabbath holy. The truth is all we've got to get out of here. There is no plan B; outside of this is death.

Let God be true and keep it as it is written; where you have no scripture, lay your hand upon your mouth.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 31:21
precepts.why:
“Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.” What are the works Paul is talking about? Not what your son did today while you were at work. One so-called leader stood up and asked a room if you go home and ask your son what his deeds were today. Who does that? He is an idiot, and whoever listens to him needs to repent.

Chronicles shows what the works are: “And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered.” The works are the works done in the service of the house of God: the sacrificial law.

Earlier in the same chapter, “Hezekiah appointed the courses of the priests and the Levites after their courses, every man according to his service, the priests and Levites for burnt offerings and for peace offerings”. Those are the works of God in the temple.

So when Paul says boasting is excluded, it means you cannot boast that you are sacrificing, as though it makes you something special, because that is done: Christ died for us. The justification is through Christ, by faith, not by the works of the temple service.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 13:11-14
precepts.why:
“Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.” What are the deeds of the law? Nehemiah shows them: “Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.” We are talking about the house of God.

“Then brought all Judah the tithe of the corn and the new wine and the oil unto the treasuries.” This is what they brought: the offerings. He “made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah”, “for they were counted faithful, and their office was to distribute unto their brethren.”

“Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for the offices thereof.” The deeds were the sacrifices and offerings he brought to the house of God.

And it is in the same chapter of Romans where God is justified in his sayings and overcomes when he is judged: let God be true, and every man a liar. This is serious. Your salvation is at hand, and a teacher who is up at the podium drinking, talking about sex and baby oil and prostitution, instead of instructing the people what these scriptures are talking about, is not a leader to lead people to God. He is a joke.

precepts.label: Sirach 44:4
precepts.why:
How do you identify a leader? Some people say you can’t say he’s not a leader. Yes, we can, because you can tell who a man is by his speech. Sirach gives the rubric: “Leaders of the people by their counsels, and by their knowledge of learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent are their instructions”.

Leaders of the people by their counsels: you should be able to tell by their godly counsel, coming from the Bible, whether or not they are leaders of the people. By their knowledge of learning meet for the people: Bishop just showed the works in Chronicles and the deeds in Nehemiah 13, proving what Romans 3 means. Wise and eloquent are their instructions.

The leaders here in Israel United in Christ prove everything they say with the scriptures. That is why I am here. Why are you there? What is your agenda? Are you there because he talks about baby oil? Are you there because he cannot break down Romans 3? The Bible is the rubric that lets us know who the real leaders are and who are not.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:15-16
precepts.why:
This is one of the first scriptures we learned when we came into this truth, elementary but important: “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” An elder has men under him who look to him for wisdom, knowledge and understanding. The brother who said a man’s deeds are what his son did today embarrassed the hell out of himself and his organization. Now he is being clowned, and because he represents the Israelite community, they label us all as stupid. precepts.why:
Paul says “For now we see through a glass, darkly”. What is the glass? Wisdom of Solomon answers it. “For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness.” Keep in mind the whole time that we are talking about the glass.

“For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Wisdom is the breath and the power of God. “For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God”. That is the glass. Wisdom is the unspotted mirror of the power of God.

“and the image of his goodness”: this Bible is the image of his goodness, his greatness. The mirror itself is unspotted, but we see into it darkly. We do not have all of it fully. We know in part and we prophesy in part, even Paul, to whom God showed incredible revelations he did not show many of the other apostles.

That is meant to humble us. We have what is needful for salvation, but there are parts of this book we do not fully understand, so you do not know as much as you think you know. When that which is perfect is come, Christ, that which is in part shall be done away, and then we shall see face to face.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:18
precepts.why:
The glass is the mirror, the unspotted image of the power of God. So why do we see it “darkly”? Ephesians answers: “Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them”.

That is what it means when it says we see through a glass darkly. We do not have the full understanding of all these scriptures. The understanding is darkened, and there is ignorance in us still.

Then go back to Corinthians: “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” When we are with Christ, he is going to make this clear to us. Until then no one should vaunt himself as if he knows it all.

So “And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.” Charity is the greatest because it is what keeps the body growing. People come in because they see how you move, how you conduct yourself and how you speak. You can teach all these scriptures with a photographic memory, but if you lack charity, if you are not kind and do not suffer long, the people will not stay.

precepts.label: Revelation 18:2-4
precepts.why:
“but rather that ye may prophesy”. The purpose of prophecy is to build your spirit up and prepare you for temptation and destruction. Prophecy is warning: thus saith the Lord. When you see these things come to pass, know that Esau, Edom, America, is the enemy the Bible speaks of.

Revelation 18 gives the warning plainly. Babylon the great is fallen and has become the habitation of devils, and the call goes out: “Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.”

Come out of religion. Come out of these doctrines. Come out of Christianity. Come out of the lies and philosophies and deceit, and repent. The Christian church has you clapping on a tambourine while the prophecy is fulfilled before your eyes; they say the book of Revelation is sealed and cannot explain any of this.

That is why we covet to prophesy: so our people can see who Babylon is, come out of her, and not receive her plagues when the fire comes on her.

The virgin means she has not been touched, defiled or destroyed, until these prophecies are fulfilled. She is going to be touched.

“for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate”. She thought she was tender and delicate, but that is coming to an end. As Daniel 2 showed, all manner of nations are within her, including her enemies: sleeper cells.

“Take the millstones, and grind meal: uncover thy locks, make bare the leg, uncover the thigh, pass over the rivers.” A virgin would be covered, but here her locks, leg and thigh are uncovered: the wickedness of Babylon, America, is being revealed.

“Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.” What shame? If your best friend is somebody in the world who just finished celebrating Christmas, you are not in the truth, and that goes for you sisters too. If we then live in hypocrisy, it is not a few stripes for us. Now is the accepted time and now is the day of salvation: are we going to waste it?

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 5:11-15
precepts.why:
“Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men”. We know the terror of the Lord, so we persuade our people to come out of the world. “For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead: And that he died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again.”

He made him to bear our sins. So did God send his Son to die so we could keep sinning in hypocrisy? He sent Christ to die for our sins, gave us his laws, and made us friends, prophets and ambassadors. That is why chapter 6 opens “We then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.” Let this word be profitable to you, so that you become prophets of God, the women bear prophets back on the earth, and the daughters are righteous.

We do not live unto ourselves. If we tell the people to come out of the world and do not live it ourselves, we were profitable to many but not to ourselves, and the punishment fits what we knew. Much is given, and much is required.

So this is our life. There is no other life outside of this: no friends in the world, nobody else to call. If you have another life where you feel comfortable, you have not been in the truth. The love of Christ constrains us to live unto him.

precepts.label: Malachi 4:1
precepts.why:
Colossians says, “Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom.” Malachi shows how deep that warning really is: “For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven.” That is why every man and every woman in this truth is warned, and why nobody is played with. “And all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble.” It is their pride and their wickedness that bring the fire on them, so you cannot be prideful. Christ died for your sin; he could have taken you out in that moment, but he gave you grace and mercy. Instead of sitting on your behind, build on the platform of Christ: go out and gather the souls Satan is oppressing, the fatherless and the widow. Brothers who want to give their rank up do not understand the work.

“And the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.” Whatever you are into, it is time to let it go before the fire comes. We fight demons every day, and sometimes it is not that you cannot do a thing; you have to command yourself to do it. Sabbath sickness is a whole slogan for brothers that are lazy bums.

So the life you used to live, the wicked life, died with Christ, giving you a chance before the fire. Now you live his life and do his work. A brother asked how to balance his life: this truth is the balance, and there is no life after it. That is the business we are in, in the classroom, on the radio, on TV and in the street: warning people of the destruction to come, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:22
precepts.why:
“For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts.” To understand who these are, go back to chapter 2, verse 22, because this is one long letter and the topic has not changed: “Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.”

The men of the last days are “lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy”, without natural affection toward their brothers and sisters, trucebreakers, false accusers. Incontinent means you are all over the place: no guideline, no law, no discipline. Fierce means angry. Traitors, heady, high-minded, “lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.”

“Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof.” Who is that? Israel, and more specifically the vessels of dishonour, the wood and the earth. You have a form of godliness, but you deny the laws of God; you follow no law. “from such turn away.” Not entertain them: turn away. God says turn away from those brothers that are dishonourable, the wood and the earth, and leave them the hell alone. In meekness you instruct those that oppose themselves, that “they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will”, but you do not walk with them.

These are the men who did not flee youthful lusts. They creep into houses and lead captive silly women: you get a silly woman who just came into the body and doesn’t know a damn thing, you crop yourself next to her and say you are her counselor now, I’m going to counsel you, sister, I got you. And she is laden with sins, led away with divers lusts.

So flee youthful lusts, and follow righteousness, faith, charity and peace with those that call on the Lord out of a pure heart. That is what separates the gold and silver from the wood and the earth. The precious sons of Zion are “comparable to fine gold”, and God said it, not man; but youthful lusts have turned the gold dim and made us earthen pitchers.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 6:12
precepts.why:
“Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.” What is our profession? We are prophets, and a prophet’s profession is to teach. All of us are supposed to be teachers. Timothy gives the charge: “Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.”

You cannot get that eternal life if you do not hold on to your profession. How are you going to fight the good fight of faith if you are not holding on to it? Your profession is to go out there and wake up our people. Your profession is to put in work, because faith without works is dead. Your first work is supposed to be in this truth, not your job. The minute we say profession, some think we mean I’m a nurse, I’m a doctor. No.

What good is it for a prophet to do nothing with it? Some of you never travel, never leave the state of Georgia, yet you say I’m a prophet. All Israel is not in Georgia; Israel is scattered to the four corners of the earth. How many of you prophets have a valid passport? Brothers have had passports since they were three. If you don’t have one, you should be ashamed. Get a passport; Donald Trump is going to force you to get one too. We have much work to do.

And “all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.” God will bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good or evil. So hold fast the profession, fight the fight, and lay hold on eternal life with a high priest who was “in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.”

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 27:5
precepts.why:
“For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth.” That correction, that chastisement, is the Lord trying your heart, seeing what your heart is made out of. Sirach ties it back to the fire: “The furnace proveth the potter’s vessels; so the trial of man is in his reasoning.”

The furnace proves the potter’s vessel, but what is the Lord proving? A man’s reasoning. When the Lord turns up the heat on your behind, he is going to try your heart. You have a couple of flat tires, you lost a job, and now you want to pick up a job on the Sabbath. Your reasoning is off, and now it is revealed: covetous. You can’t deal with your lowest state. Or you get checked, maybe it wasn’t exactly your fault, and you don’t take the low; you argue, you have strife. That is ego, and the fire revealed your thoughts.

When the potter melts the metal, each metal has a different temperature to melt and be purged. So as the fire goes up in your life, different spirits are going to come out and rise to the top. He is trying your reasoning. Are you going to deal with it or not? He is dealing with you as a son; are you going to respect him as a father?

That is why you take it cheerfully: you are getting purged as he tries your reasoning, and you get to show forth your understanding, whether everything you have been hearing is actually being learned and applied. And the trial shows other things too. Many like to suffer in silence, and the Lord is showing you your communication is weak. “Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another.” When you are going through things, lean on the brothers; call and say I am struggling in this area. Out of pride we suffer in silence, get offended with everybody, and find ourselves out the door.

If he did not love us, he would cut us off, as he cut off Esau, whom he hates. You are supposed to go through it. Three flat tires? You have one more tire than you deserve. A whole kingdom is waiting on us, the world turned right side up, and we have to push through it manfully, together, or not at all.

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:1
precepts.why:
Hebrews warns “lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you”. Where does that root come from? Proverbs answers: “He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck”. He that is often corrected hardens his neck, meaning his mind. You can't tell that brother nothing: I'm a man, you a man, I do what I want. Well, do what you want and burn by yourself.

That is the mindset of a lot of our brothers and sisters. They never took the scripture serious. Leadership corrects them, corrects them, corrects them, to the point where the correction is null and void, because they are not going to apply anything. After a while the Lord says, this spirit is rebellious as hell; he always hardens his mind and doesn't give a damn what you're saying.

You end up hardening your heart from always having correction done to you, until at the end of the day bitterness is formed, and then you're out the door with your wife and your children.

So the question for every brother and sister: are you one of the many that shall be offended when correction comes, when the men are told to get their homes in order and the women to be that pillar of rest and not stress? Or will you get in check with the Lord? The bitterness of Hebrews 12 grows out of a neck hardened against reproof.

precepts.label: Psalms 109:6-9
precepts.why:
Hebrews says “Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau”. Paul is comparing the wicked of our people to Esau, who was wicked and estranged from the womb and went to the Canaanitish women when he wanted to get married. The bitter among us become compared to Edom, and Satan becomes their daddy. Psalms shows it: “Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand.” That wicked man is Satan, the daddy of Esau and of the wicked of our people.

“When he shall be judged, let him be condemned: and let his prayer become sin.” Why does his prayer become sin? Because Christ said if you have an ought with your brother, go to him; leave your gift at the altar. You can't come to the Lord while the matter between you and your brother and your sister is not dealt with right. In 2018 there were extortioners speaking against leadership. You are not supposed to rise up against the hoary head; you are supposed to honor, and not revile the gods, your leaders. There was a lot of disrespect and dishonor.

“Let his days be few; and let another take his office. Let his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow.” That is what happens when Satan becomes your daddy. Repent.

So the profane spirit of Hebrews 12, the bitter brother or sister who turns on leadership, carries this lot. We are trying to encourage our people not to be worldly, not to keep the customs of Edom and the I-do-me, but to come back home to your people.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:17-18
precepts.why:
Christ answered Peter, “Blessed art thou, Simon Bar–jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.” Then he told him, “thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.”

How do you think that made Peter feel? Christ telling you, I am going to build my church upon you. That is what great leaders do. Good leaders make you believe in them; great leaders make you believe in you. They empower others, they strengthen others, they make you believe in yourself and not in them.

That is how a leader transfers his belief onto others, the faith Hebrews 13:7 tells us to follow. It is how the Bishop is able to raise up other bishops, raise up deacons, raise up captains, and soldiers by the thousands. Great leaders raise up more leaders.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 3:25-28
precepts.why:
Moses prayed, “I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon. But the Lord was wroth with me for your sakes, and would not hear me”. He was told, “Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter”, and to go up to the top of Pisgah and behold the land with his eyes, “for thou shalt not go over this Jordan.”

Moses could not cross over, but look at what he was charged to do: “But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him: for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which thou shalt see.” Charge him, encourage him, strengthen him.

That is your job as a leader: to encourage and strengthen the men around you. A leader transfers his belief onto the next man, so that the one coming after him can lead the people into what he himself was given to see. That is part of the faith that those who have the rule over you pass on.

precepts.label: Job 4:3
precepts.why:
“Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” Your job as a leader is to instruct many. And your job is to strengthen the weak hands.

It is your job to build the brothers and the sisters up in the spirit. That is part of how a leader transfers his belief onto others: those who have the rule over you and have spoken unto you the word of God instruct you, and when your hands are weak they strengthen them, so that you can follow their faith.

precepts.label: Luke 22:32
precepts.why:
Christ told Peter, “But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” When you convert, strengthen your brothers. That is the charge that goes with the faith that is passed on to you.

Read on and Peter answers, “Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death”, and Christ answers that before the cock crows Peter will thrice deny that he knows him. Christ prayed that Peter's faith would not fail, knowing what was coming, and still gave him the work of strengthening his brethren.

This is the leader transferring his belief onto others. Christ imparted his faith to Peter, and Peter was to impart it to the brethren. The one who has been strengthened turns around and strengthens the next man.

precepts.label: Acts 18:23
precepts.why:
“And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.” Paul went country to country strengthening all the disciples. That is the job of a leader, and it shows how a leader transfers his belief onto others.

The same work goes on today. As the bishops and the deacons trailblazed the way, the captains follow the same path, and when they go to these places they continue to build our people up worldwide. A captain just back from Guyana reports that the brothers and sisters there in South America are growing tremendously, doing real good. The Lord has good things for them.

Like Paul in Galatia and Phrygia, the leaders go out to the nations where our people are and strengthen the disciples there.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 4:17
precepts.why:
“Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known”. The Lord stood with Paul and strengthened him, so that the preaching might go forth by him.

That is our job: we must strengthen one another. You get weak at different times. You need counsel. You need some exhortation. You have to vent sometimes. And it is your job as a leader to be there to strengthen each other, as the Lord stood with Paul.

So those who have the rule over you and speak the word of God unto you are there to strengthen you, and when you are strengthened, you follow their faith and do the same for those around you.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 3:8-9
precepts.why:
This is the rebuilding of Jerusalem. “Next unto him repaired Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths. Next unto him also repaired Hananiah the son of one of the apothecaries, and they fortified Jerusalem unto the broad wall.” Each man repaired his own section of the wall. Then: “And next unto them repaired Rephaiah the son of Hur, the ruler of the half part of Jerusalem.” The ruler of the half part: he was a supervisor over that area.

That is leadership. When you come in the truth you may just edit the video, go on the fly mission, or work in the kitchen. At some point you become over the office: now you are over the brothers that are editing, over the IT team, over the building team, over the sisters. Now your job changes, because you have people under you. Everybody is not built for that level. You are not in charge; you are responsible for those in your charge. In IUIC there are different offices with leads in place, and a man who was once responsible for one office, the Lord entrusted him with more.

Sometimes brothers get overwhelmed, and that will happen. But there is no better thing than to be overwhelmed for the Lord. You do not have a demon on your back, you are not behind bars, you are not suffering illness; you are stressed out for the Lord's work, and that is a beautiful thing. So do not complain. Come up and say, I need more assistance in this office. Pray and fast for more laborers, and rejoice in it, because the Lord gave you that office and put you in that position.

precepts.label: Proverbs 11:14
precepts.why:
“Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls.” Watching for your souls is a job. Leadership is not about sitting in the front and getting the plates first. There are things you never see, never hear about and never have to deal with, because there are things put in place: the men who deal with the men, whose phones are the first ones to get called, and the senior sisters who deal with the sisters.

“Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” If you don’t follow counsel, you will fall. A congregation without counsel will fall; there is no way around it.

You have all the wisdom and understanding in front of you. If something is said to you on the phone, you can say hold on, I’ll call you right back, and reach out to a senior brother or senior sister: does this sound right? And they will tell you: no, that doesn’t sound right; no, you can’t do that; no, that’s not wise. You can alleviate a lot of situations that way. But for some reason everybody is grown: oh, I can deal with it. No, you are not in your right mind, obviously. Because of lust you ignore all the red flags, and every red flag you see before you get married is heightened a thousand times after, because you are with them every single day.

The protocol is part of that safety. No brothers should be dealing with the women on any counseling basis. The senior sisters are set up to deal with the women, and if it is a congregational issue, or somebody has to be judged, the senior sisters bring it to leadership and it is dealt with there. That multitude of counsellors is how leadership watches for your soul.

precepts.label: Sirach 32:19
precepts.why:
“Do nothing without advice; and when thou hast once done, repent not.” The ones who watch for your souls give the counsel, and you are not to move without it. Sisters, you have been given the blueprint, the things to look for when it comes to men.

When looking for a husband, you are trying to identify stability and discipline. “He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.” He is not stable; how is he going to take care of you? He is blown about with every wind of doctrine, bringing out little dumb breakdowns that did not come from leadership, like mashed potatoes on the Passover. Red flag. “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways”: one minute it’s this, the next minute it’s that. Spiritually you should never aim down; aim up for a man with more understanding than you, who can lead and guide you. If you marry a novice and you are the one teaching him to wear fringes every day, you lose respect for him, and you have married down. And don’t think you are going to change him; men typically do not look to you for counsel.

“But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” A brother barely able to feed himself, getting kicked out of apartments, lights cut off, staying at his cousin’s house, is not ready for a wife, and you are not stepping in to save a negro. God says the white man’s soul is not right, and some of you want to save him. “He is a proud man”: see how Trump talks proud and arrogant. “Neither keepeth at home”: America is never in its own country; it has military bases all over the earth, in everybody’s country, dictating and oppressing. “Who enlargeth his desire as hell, and is as death”: wherever he goes the people catch hell, and he brings death.

precepts.why:
The four angels hold the four winds “that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree”, and the cry goes out, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” So the question always comes: when are we getting out of here? By right, we want to get out. We pray every day, Lord, bring the destruction so we can leave.

Isaiah 62:7 is that prayer: “And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.” That is what we are doing. We are not to give the Lord rest until he delivers us, establishes us and makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.

But the question is, do we really want it? If we really wanted it, there would be no way we would be entertaining sin, no way we would allow evil right up under our noses while telling the Lord to hurry up. You mess around and you get slain.

The Lord has his timetable, and we are not on that level. You only see your own point of view; you do not have the Lord’s vantage point, looking at everything on this planet coming into the synchronicity he is waiting for. The angels are holding back whole armies until the sealing is finished, perhaps until that one last brother wakes up. You cannot push him. What you are responsible for is your own spirit and your own shenanigans. Get yourself right, and he will take care of the rest.

precepts.label: Sirach 36:8
precepts.why:
Here is another thing we say: make the time short, “remember the covenant, and let them declare thy wonderful works.” Lord, make the time short; remember the covenant you made with us; let the nations know you love us, tear these nations up and set us on high.

But you are not on the Lord’s level. Believe me, the Lord will not be a millisecond late when it comes to sending his angels in to destroy our enemies, and you do not know that time. So in our wanting it, what should we be doing? Making sure we are in the right spiritual and mental space, so that when he sends the angels we are not caught off guard as by a thief in the night. We want to declare his wonderful works with a hundred percent confidence, not nervous that we are still in sin somewhere that has not been found out yet.

That is why the Bible says examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith. Congregations have to examine themselves; examine your brothers and your sisters. The people who say, I don’t need to congregate, I can fellowship at home, say it because they don’t want anybody to see their nasty, wicked evil. When you come in here it is going to show, and righteous brothers and sisters are going to point it out.

Accept that correction, because it is love: the wounds of a friend rather than the kisses of an enemy. Somebody telling you where it is at will keep you out of trouble and set you right for when the Lord does send the angels. The angels are holding the four winds until the servants of God are sealed; make sure you are one of them when the time is made short.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 13:1-5
precepts.why:
Visualize the scene of Revelation 7: four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds. That wind is not the regular wind that blows every day; it is destruction. The four corners are where the militaries are, straining to get at each other, ready to press the buttons, and the angels are holding them back. Bishop Nathanyel, who is an artist, once drew this scene.

2 Esdras 13 is the same scene. “There arose a wind from the sea, that it moved all the waves thereof. And I beheld, and, lo, that man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven: and when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled that were seen under him.” That is how Christ is coming back. “And whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice, like as the earth faileth when it feeleth the fire.” If Christ is coming back with that kind of power, you think he will not see your wicked thoughts and the things you thought you were hiding? You don’t want to be on the wrong side of that magnificent coming.

“And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”. The armies are setting up to fight against our deliverer. These nations do not want Christ to save us; they want us to remain in sin and evil so they can keep subduing and destroying the Israelites.

So the Lord tells the four angels, hold the four winds; don’t let them fight yet. When Christ comes back these armies will try to fight him to keep us in slavery, and he is coming to destroy every last one of them. And if we are not right, he is going to destroy us too. Brothers and sisters, make sure your diligence is on par.

precepts.label: Sirach 39:28-31
precepts.why:
The Lord said, “I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.” How does he bring them? Sirach shows it. “All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into evil.” Then: “There be spirits that are created for vengeance, which in their fury lay on sore strokes; in the time of destruction they pour out their force, and appease the wrath of him that made them.”

God creates spirits for vengeance. The time of destruction is famine, death, plagues and wars, and in that time these spirits pour out their force, and they appease the wrath of the Lord that made them. “Fire, and hail, and famine, and death, all these were created for vengeance”, and “the sword punishing the wicked to destruction.”

So the plagues of 2 Esdras 15 do not come by chance. The Lord is behind the wars you see taking place, Russia and Ukraine, Lebanon, Israel, Palestine, Iran. When you see America bombing Iran and killing all these Palestinians, who is behind that? The Lord is behind that, working it through the spirits he created for vengeance.

precepts.label: Hebrews 1:7
precepts.why:

That is how the Lord keeps his word in 2 Esdras 15, “I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.” He does it through his angels, his ministers, a flame of fire, instigating these things in ways we cannot see.

And he says, “I will hold my tongue no more as touching their wickedness.” God is not going to be quiet any more over all the evil being done upon this earth. It starts with him putting his spirit on us and we are teaching, speaking in the ears of his people the words of prophecy, and then he comes back and deals with them the same way.

precepts.label: Revelation 16:1

Read the whole chapter and it goes into war, civil war, all of it. Who is behind it? The Lord, doing it through the angels.

They just poured some of that vial upon Trump. He came into office: get rid of DEI hiring, no more affirmative action, get rid of black history, take away citizenship from a lot of y’all. The dude is on a rampage, because God put that spirit on him, and a lot of y’all got the American dream and think this place is your rest. Trump thinks he is doing something good, bringing peace, but he is really fulfilling God’s will: bringing affliction on all nations.

May the Lord give Trump seven more years. If he is the one to fulfil God’s will, let him stay in office, even if he is the one that starts putting us to death. Let God’s will be done. Impeach him and the next president will do the same thing, because it is God’s will.

That is 2 Esdras 15 in our day: “I will bring plagues upon the world.” The Lord is the one sending them, the angels are pouring them out, and America is the one he is using to bring death and war, the same way ancient Babylon was used against the nations.

In Maccabees the brother who said let me get me a name ended up put to death.

precepts.label: Mark 4:18-19
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:23 says wisdom is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care.” Free from what care? Free from worry and stress, and above all free from the cares of this world. Mark 4 names them.

“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The cares of the world, the riches and the lusts of other things deceive you. Life does not consist in the abundance of things; they deceive you and choke the word.

Wisdom is free of those cares. The man that has wisdom is not going to be subject to the riches of this world. God said beware of covetousness, and that is wisdom, so I am going to beware of it; I am not going to entertain that.

So it is in our best interest to be paired with wisdom, because wisdom has “all power, overseeing all things.” Tether yourself to wisdom and you can see clearly, the cares of this world cannot choke the word, and it will not become unfruitful in you.

precepts.label: Hebrews 4:10-12
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 says wisdom is “the breath of the power of God.” What is the power of God? Hebrews 4 answers.

“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.” We fought that example of unbelief. If we believe, we are tethered with God and following wisdom. Wisdom is pure, steadfast and sure, and we enter into that rest.

“For the word of God is quick, and powerful.” Wisdom of Solomon 7:22 just said wisdom is “quick”, and “having all power.” The same words. And it is “sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.”

The intents of the heart are where sin begins. So we want that pure influence, so that the intents of this mind are not led astray and what guides and directs us is the word of God. There should be something in all of us that says, I can’t do that, it is wrong to do that. If we turn aside from that, we are saying we are hypocrites and don’t really believe. God has chosen us, for whatever reason, to give us wisdom. The power of God is the word of God. It is wisdom.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:7-8
precepts.why:
Wisdom is “a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Influence means to mold you and direct you. If wisdom is flowing down from the Almighty and it is influencing you, you are connected, tethered, with God. Or something else can be influencing you, and that will not be wisdom; it will be covetousness, lust, whatever it might be. Psalms 19 shows what that pure influence is.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were once simple, but wisdom is now in us, making us wise. “The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.”

That pure influence is the statutes, the laws of God. The commandment is “pure”, and it enlightens the eyes so that we can see clearly.

And if our eyes are enlightened and the Lord has converted us, what are we now? We are new, something different. That is where Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 goes: “remaining in herself, she maketh all things new.”

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 10:6
precepts.why:
Psalms 19 showed the law converting the soul, and once converted we are new. 1 Samuel 10:6 says the same thing: “And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.”

With the word of God you change into another man. That is what Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 means: “she maketh all things new.” Wisdom will make you new, so you can’t keep doing the same thing.

But if the word is dealing with you and you are still trying to live that old man, still letting that old man tell you what to do, still doing that same stuff, the Lord says, I am going to beat you with many stripes, because I gave you something and you weren’t listening. Much is given, much is required. And don’t think many stripes is a pow pow and that is it. Many in that day will say “Lord, Lord”, and he is going to say, I don’t know you.

precepts.label: Luke 6:45-49
precepts.why:
“A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.” What comes out of his mouth is what is in him.

“And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” Why are you calling me Lord, Lord, and don’t do the things I tell you to do? “Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.” “But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell.”

The one built on Christ, which is the rock, is the one that is applying it. Applying it is the whole key. That is what strengthens the foundation and lets us endure when tribulations come. Wisdom teaches us that, and it is plain to understand. In that day men will say, Lord, Lord, did not I prophesy? Yes, but you still didn’t do what I told you to do. You were out on the street teaching, but you were a hypocrite; you weren’t living it.

Brothers sometimes come up wanting to understand the deep prophecies. Brother, let’s first help you get off of Pornhub. Why are you in Revelation trying to understand these archangels? You have to let that stuff go. You know prophecy, but you don’t know you yet. Learn you, so you are able to live it, and then instruct people wisely and teach them how to serve God.

precepts.label: James 1:27
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:26: “For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness.” Wisdom is unspotted. James 1:27 shows how a man keeps himself the same way.

“Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.”

You keep yourself unspotted from the world by visiting the fatherless and the afflicted, all people afflicted in the mind. But you are too busy trying to bag the chick. She came out of the world, out of whatever she was doing, and instead of leading her to God you are trying to sleep with her.

If we want to know how to keep ourselves unspotted, we tether ourselves to God, because flowing down from him is wisdom. You come into this truth not knowing any better, wisdom flows down from God to you, you apply it, and you become new: “she maketh all things new.”

precepts.label: Sirach 4:10
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 says wisdom, “in all ages entering into holy souls, she maketh them friends of God, and prophets.” Wisdom cannot dwell in a body that is subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness or hatred. Ecclesiasticus 4:10 shows the conversion of our minds in these last days: when we put our interests over the Lord’s, it distances us from him, and when we put the Lord’s interests over ours, it brings us closer to the heavenly Father.

“Be as a father unto the fatherless, and instead of an husband unto their mother.” That is the opposite of the mindset of a whoremonger, who asks, what can I do to this sister, how can I take advantage of this single mother? The son of the Most High asks, what can I do for this young man to build him up? That is why Bishop Nathanyel says it is easier to build up a young man, a child, than to fix a broken old man; the broken old man is the one looking to take advantage.

“So shalt thou be as the son of the most High.” If you go opposite of that, you cannot be the son of the Most High. If you are looking at this sister with lustful eyes, trying to figure out how to get in her pants or take advantage of her, you can’t be the son of the Most High, and wisdom cannot dwell in you.

That is the charge on the friend of God and the prophet: to go out and raise up God’s children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy. Much is given to you, and much is going to be required of you.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 18:27
precepts.why:
Sirach says “The fear of the Lord driveth away sins”. Why? Because a person that fears God is going to keep the commandments and uphold the integrity to do the right thing, whatever situation or inconvenience he is in. Our integrity, our moral character, is directly tied to our fear toward God. It is one and the same.

Chapter 18 shows that fear at work: “A wise man will fear in every thing”. That is integrity guiding you in every step. Every step you are asking, is this the right move to make? Is this in alignment with the laws of God?

“And in the day of sinning he will beware of offence”, because he is examining himself. He has the fear of God in him and he is walking in his integrity. “But a fool will not observe time.”

The same goes for moments of correction. If you are dealing with the leadership and you cannot take the correction, if you are unable to digest it, understand it, take it and receive it, that is a sign of where your faith and your belief are.

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 15:9-17
precepts.why:
Sirach says “Let us now praise famous men” and names them as “Leaders of the people”, leaders, not one. Second Maccabees shows what those leaders do. Judas Maccabeus was preparing the men for war, and we are at war too, brothers: against sin and against our physical enemies, the children of Satan, Edom, Esau.

First a leader has to know the condition of the battle. “And so comforting them out of the law and the prophets, and withal putting them in mind of the battles that they won afore, he made them more cheerful.” If the first time you hear there is a war going on is weeks after it started, you are sleep. If you are not comforting yourself, your children, your wife and your husband out of the law and the prophets, you are not ready for the famine the Lord said is coming, when your stomach touches your back and your kids are looking at you.

“And when he had stirred up their minds, he gave them their charge, shewing them therewithal the falsehood of the heathen, and the breach of oaths.” That is why the class keeps showing that Esau is the devil, lying and breaking every treaty and oath. If your daughter secretly wants to be Tinkerbell, or wears the Frozen wig because she thinks Esau is still a princess, she does not see his breach of oaths. As a mother and a father you have to rework her mind and put her in the mindset of our fathers. Keep the body, take the mind: that was the slave master’s method, and the leader’s work is to take back the mind.

“And this was his vision”: leaders are visionaries, and where there is no vision the people perish. Onias was “a virtuous and a good man”; virtue is moral excellence, and our moral compass is God’s commandments that make us shine like gold. He was “reverend in conversation”, eloquent in speech; “gentle in condition”, keeping his composure, not hot-headed; “well spoken also”; and “exercised from a child in all points of virtue.” Nobody wakes up leading people. We are born leaders, but we become that in time. And “holding up his hands prayed for the whole body of the Jews”: leaders serve and sacrifice themselves for the betterment of the people.

Jeremias gave Judas a sword of gold: “Take this holy sword, a gift from God, with the which thou shalt wound the adversaries.” Then “Thus being well comforted by the words of Judas”: not Judas’s own mindset but the words of God, which comfort a people with a spirit of fear on them and stir them up “to valour, and to encourage the hearts of the young men.” They determined “courageously to set upon them, and manfully to try the matter by conflict.” That is the result of a great leader.

That is why the nations destroy the leaders first, because the leaders are in many cases the lifeline of the people. A leader is needed to bring comfort to a people that has been robbed, raped and murdered, and no nation on this planet needs great leaders more than ours.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 3:43
precepts.why:
Sirach praises the “Leaders of the people”, plural, and First Maccabees shows how they worked: “They said one to another, Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.” They said it one to another. Nobody tried to do it by himself. When the Bishop went to the streets, he had a reader; that is why the scriptures say go two by two. The Bishop has said for years that this work is too big for one man.

We are in that decayed estate now. The mindset of 99% of our people is in a horrible state: our women thinking they can wear tights outside and nothing is wrong, grown men going outside in a crop top with the belly out, our young women on the dance teams. If that does not put you in a different state of mind, you are destroyed. That is the urgency you see in the brothers teaching loud in the streets, and that is why the Bishop and the deacons teach the way they teach.

Restoring the decayed estate of our people is what is happening at IUSC: our women in order, our men in order, our children in order.

“Let us fight for our people”, and for the sanctuary. You will go way further for somebody else than you will for yourself, and sacrifice way more for someone else than for yourself. That is why selfish people only go so far: they are satisfied at some point. A leader’s mind is on the whole people, like the leaders Sirach praises, who left a name behind them.

precepts.label: Psalms 51:3-13
precepts.why:
Sirach says of David, “In all his works he praised the Holy One most high with words of glory; with his whole heart he sung songs, and loved him that made him.” But didn't David sin against God? He did. Yet “The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” David sinned, but David repented, and God took away his sins.

This is how he repented: “For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me. Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.” He confessed.

“Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.” And after he confessed, what did David do? “Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.” Get myself right, and then I'm going to go teach the people.

He teaches them “That all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.” Look at my example: it is good to follow the Lord, because in the end the Lord chose me as his friend.

David is a famous man, and he is an example for all of us. Some of us err in this truth, but you can recover yourself and still earn a name. You just have to do the work and be sincere. Much is given and much is required of us as leaders, so we have to be honest, confess, get clean, and then lead the people back to God.

precepts.label: Baruch 4:1-4
precepts.why:
Sirach ends the praise of Elias and Eliseus with the people after them: “Of whom some did that which was pleasing to God, and some multiplied sins.” So what is pleasing to God? Baruch answers it: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.”

Then: “O Israel, happy are we: for things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us.” The things pleasing to God are his laws. Us keeping the law is what pleases God. So when Sirach says some did that which was pleasing to God, it means some did the laws of God, and the rest multiplied sins.

That ties back to verse 10, where Elias was “ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the Lord’s judgment, before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.” That is our job, before it breaks forth, before the decree brings forth and the fierce anger of God comes, as Zephaniah 3 says: to turn our people back to God.

What is well pleasing to God is for us to keep his laws first, and then become the prophets that lead the people back to them. Much is given, much is required of us in our walk as leaders.

After Josias, the twelve prophets, Zorobabel, Neemias and Joseph, Sirach carries the line of renowned men on to the priesthood: “Simon the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again, and in his days fortified the temple”. Simon repaired the house again. Like Neemias, “who raised up for us the walls that were fallen, and set up the gates and the bars, and raised up our ruins again”, his name is tied to building back what was broken down.

That is how these renowned men earned their names. It was about building back, walking in integrity, moving right. Josias “behaved himself uprightly in the conversion of the people”, not using his position to take advantage of the people or handling the word of God deceitfully. Neemias raised the walls and established the laws again, so nobody would come in trying to get our people to shop on the Sabbath. Simon repaired and fortified the house of God.

So it is with us: “in the time of the ungodly he established the worship of God.” In the midst of all this debauchery we are to establish the worship of God, with no hypocrisy, no covetousness and no murmuring, so that the people see us and say these are those guys we heard about that are going to come back on the earth. That is how you become the famous man.

The class only jumped through these chapters for time’s sake. Go through Sirach 44 to 50 again on your own, because there is a lot more in them.
